summary.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR122 crore (from INR135 crore) and EBITDA/MT to INR20,114; Q1 FY27 guided to high end of 6-8% volume growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by West Asia war disruptions to logistics, feedstock availability and customer ordering, with Egypt operations stalled through March. EBITDA declined year-on-year to INR122 crore and EBITDA per metric ton to INR20,114 from INR21,715. India volumes grew 8% YoY in Q4 while AMET volumes fell 15% and RoW fell 7%, with the Americas a relative bright spot after US tariff reversals. Management guided only for Q1 FY27 (high end of 6-8% volume growth and high end of INR19,000-21,000/MT EBITDA), declining to give full-year guidance given the uncertainty.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volumes up 8% YoY in Q4; Performance up 3% and Specialty up over 27%. Full-year growth held despite reformulation pressure from key Tier 1 customers, offset by non-Tier 1 and D2C accounts.

segments.name: AMET (Africa, Middle East, Turkey)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 15% YoY in Q4, mainly supply-led via Galaxy Chemicals Egypt raw material and transhipment disruption in March. Management said Jan-Feb growth would have been about 2-3%; the segment is still underperforming versus its prior ~90,000 MT ambition, now about 60,000 MT base.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Volumes down 7% YoY in Q4 (double-digit growth through Q3) due to delayed shipments to Europe and LatAm, freight spikes and repricing; full-year growth was 4%.

segments.name: Americas / US
segments.commentary: Relative bright spot; volumes improved sequentially after tariff reversals. TRI-K premium specialty business performed consistently well, though specialty revenue was flat QoQ due to product mix.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: volume growth at the higher end of the 6-8% guided range, conditional on current conditions not worsening.
Q1 FY27: EBITDA per MT at the higher end of the INR19,000-21,000 range.
No full-year FY27 or FY28 volume or revenue guidance given; management said clarity expected at Q1 results in August.
India: 8-10% volume growth possible if demand holds; risks include monsoon, energy-price-driven inflation and discretionary spending.
Long-term specialty mix: management expects 60:40 to 65:35 (performance:specialty) even by 2031. Analyst Day target of about INR25,000/MT is backloaded to FY27-FY30.
Growth capex: no major new growth capex committed in FY27 beyond work-in-progress capitalisation and routine brownfield/replacement capex; maintenance capex about INR20-30 crore per year.
capex_capacity: Capex of roughly INR480 crore over the last 3 years, mostly growth capex in Specialty Ingredients; a major portion commissioned in the last 1.5 years, so benefits begin to show from FY26-27.
Maintenance capex about INR20-30 crore per year.
Product launches include Galsoft Lumithic (amino acid-based self-thickening mild surfactant) shown at in-cosmetics Paris.
Management said the company has spare flexibility to gain volume share from supply-constrained competitors, and is already producing an alternative product in India.
EPC/project income recognised on a percentage-of-completion basis; not material in FY26, with bulk expected in FY27.
demand_pricing: Feedstock costs rose sharply in Q4 due to the geopolitical situation; petrochemical feedstocks rose more than oleochemicals, and fatty alcohol prices have more than doubled per management, with availability the main issue.
Ethylene oxide and sulfur prices rising frequently; supply managed through vendor partnerships; management said it was not seeing major supply worries.
Pricing is passed on with a lag of about a month because customers expect price stability; freight-cost increases were also passed through to customers.
Management sees no panic buying in Q4; demand described as healthy in India and AMET/Africa/Turkey, with monitoring of inflation-driven demand weakness.
Competitive pressure in AMET from local players that are backward integrated, who have taken share from global customers.
Mix benefits expected from Americas specialty and Europe project pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why was specialty revenue flat QoQ (INR493 crore to INR498 crore) despite US tariff reversal, and how big is India's specialty mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat QoQ figure to product mix in US Q4 as products were shifted after tariff reversal. India specialty base is small, but D2C brands are growing their presence and use specialty ingredients.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term specialty mix outlook and the outlook for FY27-28 volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to grow both segments, expects a 60:40 to 70:30 range depending on performance, and still sees 60:40 to 65:35 by 2031. No FY27-28 volume guidance beyond Q1 given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and pass-through, and the risk of down-trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through is possible with a lag of about 1 month. Petrochemical feedstocks have risen more than oleochemicals, and the current challenge is supply availability rather than demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Egypt facility's status on raw materials, logistics and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand not a challenge; March was disrupted by stuck inbound materials. Operations restored from mid-April, and management expects May and June to run uninterrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Q1 volume guidance rely mainly on supply constraints at competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; the guidance is driven by India recovery to 8-10% growth, US business revival and AMET supply recovery, with a caveat that the outlook holds only if current conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AMET fallen from ~90,000 MT to ~60,000 MT and what is the market outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Local backward-integrated players gained share; Egypt plant idle in March. Management said AMET has likely bottomed, with market growth of about 3-4%.

risks_watch: Logistics: port congestion and elongated transit times persist even as congestion eases; freight rates elevated.

Raw material availability: sulfur and ethylene oxide (ethylene-based supply concentrated in one supplier) and petrochemical feedstock availability; West Asia escalation (Strait of Hormuz) could worsen.
Demand: inflationary energy prices could curb discretionary consumer spending and customer production cuts in high season (Jan-Sep).
AMET: continued share loss to local players, currency and inflation issues in Egypt and Turkey, and credit risk in certain markets.
Q1 FY27 results in August: whether volume growth reaches the high end of 6-8% and EBITDA/MT reaches INR21,000.
Possible grammage reduction by FMCG customers as a substitute price increase, which could weigh on volumes.
Wellness segment progress, described by management as behind plan.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and guarded on outlook: management confident on Q1 volume and India demand but repeatedly declined to give full-year or FY27-28 guidance, citing uncertainty. Tone was defensive on AMET and RoW decline, attributing it mainly to supply and logistics issues rather than demand.
key_quotes: Barring any new unforeseen events, we are confident that performance in the coming quarters will improve sequentially.
Q1, we are looking that you'll be able to -- we'll be delivering close to the higher end of the volume guidance range of 6% to 8%.
The issue is not about demand side, I think more on the availability of raw materials to take care of supplies.
So even by 2031, I do not see it's going, say, probably in the zone of 60%-40%, 65%-35%.

growth.why: Management guided only Q1 FY27 volume growth at the high end of 6-8% and EBITDA/MT at the high end of INR19,000-21,000, conditional on conditions not worsening, with no full-year FY27 guidance; backing is partial (spare flexibility and recently commissioned Specialty capex, no quantified new orders), and growth capex is largely halted beyond WIP capitalisation.
